source_text: Hanc ergo tu in parvulis criminosam, vitiosam et damnatam voluntate sua arguis an conditione nascendi? Si propria voluntate, ut videlicet illi parvuli suis studiis peccasse dicantur, monstrum quidem opinionis exoritur, peccati tamen tradux negatur, non enim accepit ab alio, quod potuit ipse committere; sin autem tot mala non actione sua, sed conditione sortitur, naturaliter iniqua convincitur.
pass_a_gloss: This therefore in little ones do you argue criminal, vicious and condemned by its own will or by the condition of being born? If by own will, so that namely those little ones are said to have sinned by their studies, a monster indeed of opinion arises, yet the vine-layer of sin is denied, for he has not received from another what he himself could commit; but if it is allotted so many evils not by its action but by condition, it is convicted naturally unjust.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis

pass_b_english: Do you therefore charge this nature in infants with being criminal, corrupt, and condemned because of its own will or because of the condition of birth? If through its own will—so that those infants are said to have sinned by their own efforts—a monstrous opinion arises, but inherited sin is denied: someone did not receive from another what he could commit himself. But if it receives so many evils not by its own action but by its condition, it is proved naturally unjust.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
